Central Question: How do FEMA disaster relief claims associated with Hurricane Helene correspond to social vulnerability data for impacted counties in NC? 

Supporting Questions: 
-Which counties in NC sustained the most building damage based on FEMA claims? 
-How do the overall SVI scores compare for those 10 counties? 
-How do the percentile rankings for each SVI sub-theme compare for the top 10 counties?
-What is the correlation between overall SVI percentiles and building damage? 

Variables: 
buildingDamageAmount- (dollars) 
countyCode- (numeric code)
RPL_THEME1- (percentile) Percentile ranking for Socioeconomic Status theme summary  
RPL_THEME2- (percentile) Percentile ranking for Household Characteristics theme summary 
RPL_THEME3- (percentile) Percentile ranking for Racial and Ethnic Minority Status theme 
RPL_THEME4- (percentile) Percentile ranking for Housing Type/ Transportation theme 
RPL_THEMES- (percentile) Overall percentile ranking 
```{r setup}
#install.packages("here")
library(readr)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
#loading appropriate packages
setwd(here())
getwd() 
#setting the wroking directory
FEMA_SVI_data <- read_csv(here
("data/processed/master_FEMA_SVI_data.csv"))
```

```{r figure fema}
tencounties_highest_claims <- c(37021, 37111, 37089, 37011, 37023,37115, 37009, 
                       37161, 37087, 37189)

FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(countyCode),y = buildingDamageAmount,
             color = factor(countyCode))) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Building Damage Amount by Top 10 County Codes FEMA Claim",
    x = "FIPS County Code", y = "Building Damage Amount ($)",
    color = "County Code") + theme_classic() +
    scale_color_discrete(labels = c(                                             
      #allows me to assign name to each code in legend
    "37021 = Buncombe",
    "37111 = Mcdowell",
    "37089 = Henderson",
    "37011 = Avery",
    "37009 = Ashe",
    "37115 = Madison",
    "37023 = Burke",
    "37161 = Rutherford",
    "37087 = Haywood",
    "37189 = Watauga")) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 2000000))
```

```{r figure svi total}
FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(COUNTY %in% SVI_tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  distinct(COUNTY, RPL_THEMES) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(COUNTY),
             y = RPL_THEMES,
             fill = factor(COUNTY))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Overall Social Vulnerability Rating of Top 10 Most Damaged Counties",
    x = "County",
    y = "Overall Social Vulnerability Index (0-1)",
    fill = "County"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      vjust = 1,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
   
    
```

```{r summary table}
#creating summary table
summary_table <- FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  group_by(countyCode, COUNTY, RPL_THEMES) %>% 
  summarize(total_building_damage = sum(buildingDamageAmount, na.rm = TRUE), 
            .groups = "drop_last") %>% 
  #adding the building damage amount per county 
  select(countyCode, COUNTY, total_building_damage, RPL_THEMES) %>%
  as_tibble()

#changing column names to be more informative  
colnames(summary_table) <- c("FIPS County Code", "County", "Building Damage Amount ($)", 
                             "Overall Social Vulnerabilty Index (0-1)")
#view table
summary_table
    
```

```{r per capita table}

#Adding column to dataframe that has net building payment amount per capita using estimated total population column 
FEMA_SVI_PER_CAPITA <- FEMA_SVI_data %>% mutate(ratio = netBuildingPaymentAmount/E_TOTPOP) %>% rename ("NetBuildingPaymentPerCapita" = "ratio")

```

```{r figure with net building payment amount}

tencounties_highest_claims <- c(37021, 37111, 37089, 37011, 37023,37115, 37009, 
                       37161, 37087, 37189)

#building damage top ten counties
FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(countyCode),y = netBuildingPaymentAmount,
             color = factor(countyCode))) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Building Damage Amount by Top 10 County Codes FEMA Claim",
    x = "FIPS County Code", y = "Building Damage Amount ($)",
    color = "County Code") + theme_classic() +
    scale_color_discrete(labels = c(                                             
      #allows me to assign name to each code in legend
    "37021 = Buncombe",
    "37111 = Mcdowell",
    "37089 = Henderson",
    "37011 = Avery",
    "37009 = Ashe",
    "37115 = Madison",
    "37023 = Burke",
    "37161 = Rutherford",
    "37087 = Haywood",
    "37189 = Watauga")) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 900000))

```
```{r summary table with all SVI variables}

#creating summary table 2 with net building payment amount, per capita building payment amount, and all SVI vulnerability indices 

summary_table_2 <- FEMA_SVI_PER_CAPITA %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  group_by(countyCode, COUNTY, RPL_THEMES, RPL_THEME1, RPL_THEME2, RPL_THEME3, RPL_THEME4) %>%  
  #adding the building payment amount per county and per capita ratio
  summarize(total_building_payment = sum(netBuildingPaymentAmount, na.rm = TRUE), 
            total_building_payment_per_capita = sum(netBuildingPaymentAmount, na.rm = 
                                                    TRUE)/first(E_TOTPOP), .groups =
                                                    "drop_last") %>% 
  select(countyCode, COUNTY, total_building_payment, total_building_payment_per_capita,
         RPL_THEMES, RPL_THEME1, RPL_THEME2, RPL_THEME3, RPL_THEME4) %>%
  as_tibble()

#changing column names to be more informative  
colnames(summary_table_2) <- c("FIPS County Code", "County", "Net Building Payment Amount ($)", "Net Building Payment Amount per capita", "Overall Social Vulnerability Index (0-1)", "Socioeconomic Vulnerability (0-1)", "Household Characteristic Vulnerability (0-1)", "Racial/Ethnic Minority Vulnerability (0-1)", "Housing Type/Transportation Vulnerability")
#view table 2
summary_table_2


#creating summary table for SVI percentile rankings 

SVI_summary_table <- FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(COUNTY %in% SVI_tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  select(COUNTY, RPL_THEMES, RPL_THEME1, RPL_THEME2, RPL_THEME3, RPL_THEME4) %>%
  distinct(COUNTY, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(COUNTY)
  
colnames(SVI_summary_table) <- c("County", "Overall
                               Social Vulnerability Index (0-1)", "Percentile Ranking of Socioeconomic Status (0-1)", "Percentile Ranking of Household Characteristics (0-1)", "Percentile Ranking of Racial/Ethnic
                               Minority Status (0-1)", "Percentile Ranking for Housing Type/Transportation (0-1)")

SVI_summary_table
    
```
```{r linear regression}

#linear regression overall SVI
SVI_regression <- lm(`Overall Social Vulnerability Index (0-1)` ~ `Net Building Payment Amount per capita`, data = summary_table_2)

summary(SVI_regression)
plot(SVI_regression)

#linear regression socioeconomic 
socioecon_regression <- lm(`Socioeconomic Vulnerability (0-1)` ~ `Net Building Payment Amount per capita`, data = summary_table_2)

summary(socioecon_regression)
plot(socioecon_regression)

#linear regression racial/ethnic minority
racialethnic_regression <- lm(`Racial/Ethnic Minority Vulnerability (0-1)` ~ `Net Building Payment Amount per capita`, data = summary_table_2)

summary(racialethnic_regression)
plot(racialethnic_regression)
     
#linear regression household
household_regression <- lm(`Household Characteristic Vulnerability (0-1)` ~ `Net Building Payment Amount per capita`, data = summary_table_2)

summary(household_regression)
plot(household_regression)

#linear regression housing type
housingtypetransportation_regression <- lm(`Housing Type/Transportation Vulnerability` ~ `Net Building Payment Amount per capita`, data = summary_table_2)

summary(housingtypetransportation_regression)
plot(housingtypetransportation_regression)

```

```{r correlation overall}
ggplot(summary_table_2, aes(x = `Net Building Payment Amount per capita`,
y = `Overall Social Vulnerability Index (0-1)`)) +
#x=net building amount per capita for each county, y= Overall vuln for top 10 counties 
  geom_point(aes(color = County), size = 5) +
geom_smooth(method = "lm",formula = y ~ x, color = "black") +
#adding the lines of best fit  
  stat_regline_equation(
  aes(label = after_stat(eq.label)),
  label.x = min(summary_table_2$`Net Building Payment Amount per capita`),
  label.y = 0.98
) +
    #adds the line of best fit equation to graph;
#used chatgpt to figure out what code would do this
stat_cor(
  aes(label = after_stat(r.label)),
  label.x = min(summary_table_2$`Net Building Payment Amount per capita`),
  label.y = 0.90
) +
    #adds the r correlation value to graph;
stat_cor(
  aes(label = after_stat(rr.label)),
  label.x = min(summary_table_2$`Net Building Payment Amount per capita`),
  label.y = 0.80
) +
#used chatgpt to figure out what code would do this
labs(title = "Building Payment per Capita vs. Overall Social Vulnerability", x = expression("Net Building Payment Amount per Capita ($)"),
y = expression("Overall Social Vulnerability Index (0-1)")) +
#plot labels
coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) #zooming in to where the bulk of data is for visibility

```
```{r}
vulnerability_data <- summary_table_2 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      `Socioeconomic Vulnerability (0-1)`,
      `Racial/Ethnic Minority Vulnerability (0-1)`),
    names_to = "Vulnerability_Type",
    values_to = "Vulnerability_Score") 
#assigning values to one dataframe so I can plot two vulnerabilities at once

vulnerability_data <- vulnerability_data %>%
  mutate(
    Vulnerability_Type = factor(
      Vulnerability_Type,
      levels = c(
        "Socioeconomic Vulnerability (0-1)",
        "Racial/Ethnic Minority Vulnerability (0-1)"
      )
    )
  )
#used ChatGPT to troubleshoot

ggplot(vulnerability_data,
       aes(x = `Net Building Payment Amount per capita`,
           y = Vulnerability_Score,
           color = Vulnerability_Type)) +
geom_point(aes(color = Vulnerability_Type), size = 5) +
#making points by vulnerability type and points large for visibility
geom_smooth(method = "lm",
              formula = y ~ x,
              aes(color = Vulnerability_Type),
              se = FALSE) +
#adding both lines at once
labs(
    title = "Building Payment per Capita vs. Socioeconomic & Racial/Ethnic Vulnerability",
    x = "Net Building Payment Amount per Capita ($)",
    y = "Vulnerability Index (0-1)",
    color = "Vulnerability Type") +
scale_color_discrete(
  labels = c("Socioeconomic Vulnerability",
    "Racial/Ethnic Minority Vulnerability"))+
#needed to assign specific lables because there are spaces in the df for some reason
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))+
#capping the y-axis from 0-1 because that's the possible values of the index
stat_regline_equation(
  aes(label = after_stat(eq.label), color = Vulnerability_Type),
  label.x = min(vulnerability_data$`Net Building Payment Amount per capita`),
  label.y = c(0.98, 0.83)) +
stat_cor(
  aes(label = after_stat(r.label), color = Vulnerability_Type),
  label.x = min(vulnerability_data$`Net Building Payment Amount per capita`),
  label.y = c(0.93, 0.78)) +
stat_cor(
  aes(label = after_stat(rr.label), color = Vulnerability_Type),
  label.x = min(vulnerability_data$`Net Building Payment Amount per capita`),
  label.y = c(0.88, 0.75)
)
#adds the line of best fit and r correlation value to graph;
#used chatgpt to figure out what code would do this
  
```
